quote: There is no foreign land; it is the traveller only that is foreign, and now and again, by a flash of recollection, lights up the contrasts of the earth.
source: Robert Louis Stevenson, The Silverado Squatters, Part II, With the Children of Israel, chapter III, The Return (Chatto and Windus, 1883)
note: The locator was corrected. The sentence is not in The Scot Abroad; it closes a paragraph in The Return, the third chapter of Part II, With the Children of Israel, in the 1883 Chatto and Windus first edition. The wording is the edition's own.

evidence.where: The 1883 Chatto and Windus first edition, read in the archive.org OCR scan, where the sentence falls under the heading The Return; cross-checked against the Project Gutenberg text (etext 516), which places it the same way
evidence.edition: The Silverado Squatters, Chatto and Windus, London, 1883
evidence.locator: Part II, With the Children of Israel, chapter III, The Return, the paragraph on incongruous memories

reason: The wording is exact in the first edition, semicolon and British traveller included, but the chapter was wrong: the line sits in The Return in Part II, not in The Scot Abroad in Part I. A standard reference line, gentle enough for the month. Not shipped, Stevenson at zero of three.
